copy.title: The Murdoch Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Rupert Murdoch’s family: who controls Fox and News Corp, the trust fight and its $3.3 billion settlement, which stocks you can buy, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #016 · The Murdoch family · Data as of
copy.h1: Four children had a vote. Now one does. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, who controls Fox and News Corp, which of their companies you can buy stock in, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. Rupert has six children; the two youngest are counted, not mapped.
copy.investLede: Two family companies trade on the stock market: Fox Corp and News Corp. Each has two share classes, and the family’s control runs through the Class B shares.
copy.moneyLede: Forbes counts one fortune for Rupert and his family. It doesn’t publish separate figures for the children.
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in SEC filings, the trust settlement and the big deals. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From one Adelaide newspaper in 1952 to Fox, The Wall Street Journal and a $3.3 billion family settlement.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what the Murdochs have

summary.t: Turned the Adelaide newspaper he inherited into a global media business that includes Fox News, The Wall Street Journal, the New York Post and The Times of London. He stepped down as chairman of Fox and News Corp in 2023.

owns.t: Chairman emeritus since stepping down in 2023. Since the 2025 settlement he has no direct voting control.
Chairman emeritus. News Corp owns the New York Post, which he bought in 1976, and The Wall Street Journal.
Sold most of it, including the movie studio, FX and National Geographic, to Disney for $71.3 billion in 2019.

record.t: Set up in 1999 after his divorce from Anna Torv. Rupert controlled four votes and each of his four eldest children had one. His two youngest children share in the money but have no vote.

In late 2023 he asked a Nevada probate court to change the trust so Lachlan alone would control it after his death. A probate commissioner rejected the change in December 2024, and Rupert’s lawyer said they would appeal.
Prudence, Elisabeth and James left the trust for about $1.1 billion each. A new family company, LGC Holdco, holds the voting stake, and Lachlan alone votes it until 2050.

facts.t: Married five times: to Patricia Booker, Anna Torv, Wendi Deng, Jerry Hall and, in 2024, Elena Zhukova.
Became a US citizen in 1985 to meet the legal requirement for owning US TV stations.
Forbes estimated in 2025 that the Disney shares from the Fox sale could be worth nearly $6 billion if the family still holds them.
Bought a Montana ranch for $200 million in 2021.

kidsNote.t: Rupert has six children with three of his wives. This map follows the four eldest; the two youngest, his daughters with Wendi Deng, are counted here but not mapped.

summary.t: A retired molecular biologist. She married Rupert in June 2024 at his California estate. It is his fifth marriage.
Rupert’s eldest child, from his first marriage. Sat on the board of Times Newspapers from 2010 to 2022. Lives in Sydney.

record.t: Left the family trust in September 2025 for about $1.1 billion. Under the deal she must sell any Fox or News Corp shares she holds herself within six months.
Joined Elisabeth and James in opposing Rupert’s bid to change the trust in Lachlan’s favor.

summary.t: Managing director of Sky Networks in the late 1990s. Founded the TV producer Shine in 2001 and co-founded the production company Sister in 2019.

owns.t: Co-founded in 2019 with Jane Featherstone and Stacey Snider.
Founded in 2001. News Corp bought it in 2011.

record.t: Left the family trust in September 2025 for about $1.1 billion.

facts.t: Appointed CBE in 2022 for services to diversity in the arts and to charity.

summary.t: Executive chair and CEO of Fox Corp since 2019 and chair of News Corp since his father retired in 2023. Since the 2025 settlement he alone votes the shares the family company, LGC Holdco, holds in both.

owns.t: Executive chair and CEO since March 2019.
His private investment company, founded in 2005. It owns the Australian radio group Nova Entertainment.

record.t: Votes the shares held by LGC Holdco, which is owned by trusts for him and his two youngest half-sisters: about 36.2% of Fox’s Class B voting stock and 33.1% of News Corp’s.
Forbes said in September 2025 that the trusts he controls hold about $6.6 billion of Fox and News Corp shares, which likely makes him a billionaire.

facts.t: Bought a Bel Air, Los Angeles, mansion for $150 million in 2019.

summary.t: CEO of 21st Century Fox from 2015 to 2019. Resigned from News Corp’s board in July 2020, citing disagreements over editorial content and strategy. Runs his own investment company, Lupa Systems.

owns.t: His investment company. Holds stakes in Tribeca Enterprises and in MCH Group, which owns Art Basel. Agreed in May 2026 to buy New York magazine, Vox.com and the Vox Media Podcast Network for about $300 million.
CEO from 2015 until Disney bought most of the company in 2019.

record.t: Left the family trust in September 2025 for about $1.1 billion.

facts.t: Dropped out of Harvard and started a record label, Rawkus Records.
